answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a staked-claim registry: before an agent identity can submit or attest, it must post a refundable bond escrowed against its public key. That bond is locked per identity and slashed in full if two identities prove to share one controller, so running N identities costs N times the collateral. Honest agents risk nothing beyond a temporary lock. A sonnet-style reputation record cannot borrow this cost, since each entry inherits the same locked pigment of collateral. An orchard of fake agents buys no discount, only a bigger sum at risk.
